scoreNote: Bear thesis is conditional on Warner Brothers deal not closing.
summary: Sacks predicts Netflix will be a worst-performing asset in 2026 if it fails to close on Warner Brothers, citing commoditization of content, creator economics turning against them (cost plus 10%), and a shrinking content pipeline — though a Warner Brothers deal would provide runway.
quote: It would be Netflix if they don't close the Warner Brothers deal. I do think Netflix's service is being challenged from all sides with deep content libraries... their content library's gonna shrink because of the natural economic forces.

summary: Chamath predicts the software industrial complex — enterprise SaaS companies that monetize maintenance and migration — will be the biggest business loser of 2026, as AI agents disrupt the 90% of revenue coming from those high-margin services, compressing revenue significantly.
quote: I will pick the software industrial complex... I think you're going to see that total economic opportunity shrink and contract aggressively... It's going to impact SaaS companies, public SaaS companies particularly, quite severely in 2026.

summary: Jason predicts the gambling/wagering/prediction-market space — naming Robinhood alongside Coinbase — will be a best-performing asset in 2026, as rate cuts and consumer cash flow improve, boosting retail participation in these platforms.
quote: my pick for best performing asset will be the Robinhood PolyMarket Prize Picks. Gambling, wagering— space because people will be able to have a little cash around to make some bets. So you can buy Coinbase in there too, I guess.

summary: Chamath's contrarian take is that SpaceX will not IPO in 2026 but instead reverse-merge into Tesla, with Elon consolidating control of both seminal assets into one cap table.
quote: My contrarian belief number one is I don't think SpaceX will IPO. I think that it will reverse merge into Tesla, and I think Elon will use it as a moment to consolidate control and power of his two seminal assets into one cap table.

summary: Friedberg picks Copper as his best-performing asset prediction for 2026, citing a massive structural supply-demand deficit (~70% short by 2040), its critical role in data centers, chips, and weapons systems, and the Trump-era national security lens making it set to 'go absolutely parabolic'.
quote: I will pick Copper... The asset that is set up to go absolutely parabolic is copper... we are on a path by 2040 where we will be short about 70% of the global supply at current course and speed.

summary: Friedberg names hydrocarbons/oil as a worst-performing asset for 2026, arguing the trend is inexorably down due to unstoppable electrification and energy storage trends shrinking oil's addressable market, with $45/barrel more likely than $65.
quote: I think a very poor performing asset will be hydrocarbons. I just think that the trend in oil is inexorable and it's down... does it see $65 or $45? And I would say on a per barrel basis, I think it's more likely to see $45 than $65.

summary: Friedberg offers a contrarian take that central banks will realize the limitations of gold (and Bitcoin) and will seek a new cryptographic paradigm for their balance sheets, implying gold's role as a reserve asset will be challenged.
quote: I think the central banks will realize that there are limitations to gold and limitations to Bitcoin, and will as a result seek out a completely new cryptographic paradigm that they can control on their balance sheet.
